records.technology: Java4Shell / HotSpot Base64; PaperCut NG/MF; Netwrix Data Classification; Fusion
records.event: Downstream vendor remediation and exposure advisories
records.summary: Java4Shell has demonstrated application-specific remote code execution. PaperCut and Netwrix published fixed bundled runtimes; Lucidworks disclosed affected Fusion deployments and interim mitigation.
records.impact: Potential Java process compromise, secret disclosure and service disruption; product-specific exploitability varies.
records.action: Inventory actual bundled runtimes and CPU capabilities; upgrade PaperCut to 26.0.7 and Netwrix to 5.8.0.38; follow Lucidworks mitigation; patch JDK and restart JVMs. Where supported temporarily disable Base64 intrinsics.
records.hunt: Review JVM crashes, unusual Java child processes, outbound connections, anomalous authentication and configuration changes; preserve logs and rotate exposed secrets if compromise suspected.
records.affected: Unpatched OpenJDK 17.0.6+ and affected 21/25/27 on x86-64 AVX-512 VBMI where untrusted input reaches decoder; Oracle Java 8 Performance Pack exception. PaperCut 25.0.0-25.0.13 and 26.0.0-26.0.6 Application/Site Servers; Fusion 5.9.9+ and some earlier 5.x updated api-gateway images; Netwrix bundled JRE.
records.fixed: Oracle 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1, 8u513-perf; PaperCut 26.0.7; Netwrix 5.8.0.38. Fusion patched builds pending per Nov 24 advisory.
records.notes: CVSS v4.0 9.2 researcher rating. Active exploitation claimed in a commercial press release without supporting telemetry; not independently confirmed. RCE demonstrations are not proof of exploitation of each downstream product. PaperCut 25.x fix pending per advisory.
records.sla: 24–72 hours; immediate assessment of internet-facing identity and CI/CD

records.event: Splunk publishes defensive analytics for demonstrated Ruby2Shell exploitation path
records.summary: Ruby case-conversion heap overflow can be reached before authentication in default Rails and classic Sinatra; researchers report demonstrated RCE. Splunk released hunting analytics.
records.impact: Application worker compromise, data theft or service disruption.
records.action: Upgrade Ruby to 3.3.14, 3.4.13 or 4.0.10 and restart/redeploy workers and images; migrate EOL Ruby.
records.hunt: Use Splunk Ruby2Shell analytics; correlate suspicious web requests, Ruby worker crashes, unexpected child processes and outbound connections. A request match alone does not prove compromise.
records.affected: Affected Ruby releases from 2.4; 3.3 before 3.3.14, 3.4 before 3.4.13, 4.0 before 4.0.10; older branches EOL.
records.notes: Legacy single-byte encoding case conversion causes heap corruption. Public remote RCE PoC release not verified; no confirmed malicious exploitation established.

records.evidence: Researcher-demonstrated local SYSTEM escalation; commercial exploit available
records.summary: Core Security documented a demonstrated local privilege escalation through unsafe DLL loading by a privileged Windows Remote Access service. Its commercial exploit was listed November 19; the detailed write-up was reported published November 23.
records.impact: Local attacker can obtain SYSTEM, compromise protected data and establish persistence.
records.action: Install November 10 Windows security updates or later applicable cumulative updates; verify OS builds.
records.hunt: Investigate privileged svchost.exe loading unsigned or unexpected DLLs from user-writable locations, anomalous RAS activity and suspicious child processes.
records.affected: Affected Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server releases; local low-privilege code execution required.
records.fixed: Release-specific November 2026 updates; examples Windows 10 22H2 build 19045.7846, Windows 11 25H2 build 26200.9974, Server 2022 build 20348.5870.
records.notes: Not remote unauthenticated access. No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation. Detailed researcher blog inaccessible directly (403); primary commercial exploit listing verified.
records.sla: Assess immediately; target 72 hours for high-risk systems

records.event: Calif publishes demonstrated Tor Browser deanonymisation chain
records.evidence: Researcher demonstration; public technical PoC; no confirmed active exploitation established
records.summary: Calif demonstrated one-click public-source IP disclosure against Tor Browser 15.0.22 on Linux using a Gecko use-after-free and privileged browser navigation.
records.impact: Loss of network anonymity; potential source, journalist or activist exposure. Full parent-process code execution was not demonstrated.
records.action: Update Tor Browser to a current supported release; verify Firefox ESR patch levels and restrict direct egress on high-risk anonymity workstations.
records.hunt: Review authorised endpoint and network telemetry for unexpected direct browser egress, suspicious page visits and browser crashes; preserve evidence if suspected.
records.affected: Demonstrated on Tor Browser 15.0.22, Linux, default settings; broader version scope requires vendor validation.
records.fixed: Tor Browser 15.0.23 reported as fixed; use current supported release.
records.notes: User interaction required. Research publication 26 November; original fix predates baseline. No independent retest performed.
records.sla: Proposed: inventory within 24 hours; update high-risk users within 24 hours, others within 72 hours
